summary: Lock-Score Governor fixes validated end-to-end (backend only). 11/11 pytest cases pass. GET /api/picks/today returns NBA/NHL/Soccer picks (counts: Soccer=56, NHL=25, NFL=43, MLB=17, CFB=5, NBA=3). NHL alt-goal cap invariant holds: 0 NHL `Over N.5 Goals` (N>=1) picks with lock_score>=85 remain in canonical_picks; 20+ sampled rows show lock=84.9 with nhl_alt_goal_cap_applied=True (Timo Meier, Jesper Bratt, Arseny Gritsyuk Over 1.5 Goals all correctly capped). NBA ALT LOCK floor invariant holds: scanned 540 canonical NBA picks, 104 qualifying (ALT LOCK with wp>=70 & edge>=0), 0 offenders below the min(96, 60+wp*40) floor. Hartenstein Over 4.5 Points · ALT LOCK canonical regression confirmed at lock=96.0 (wp=90.28, edge=9.18, floor_applied=True). Soccer soft-pass logic correct: scanned 500 off_board Soccer player-props, 0 flagged via roster_unverified/roster_conflict alone (all off_board rows carry a hard-reject reason). Soccer published locks >=85 count = 6969 (well above the 260 baseline). NFL leakage cap + NFL reliability floor code blocks still present in services/pick_refresh_orchestrator.py (no regression).
critical_code_review_comments: pick_refresh_orchestrator.py post-processing blocks for NHL alt-goal cap, NHL anytime-scorer floor, and NBA ALT LOCK floor use the same wp-based reliability formula (60 + wp*40, capped at 96). Logic is consistent and symmetric with the existing NFL reliability floor pattern.

Both the orchestrator-level and publication-level Soccer gates share the same _HARD_REJECT_REASONS set across services/publication_helpers.py (line 410-414) and services/prediction_publication_service.py (line 509-513) — good DRY alignment; consider extracting to a shared constant later.
Note on backend/.env line 78 — CANONICAL_IMPORT_ENABLED has stray leading whitespace (`"    true"`). Likely benign (parsed as truthy string) but tidy up to `true` to avoid future surprise.
